title: Less Is Fair: Reducing RTT Unfairness Through Buffer Sizing
author: Agnieszka Piotrowska
status: eligibility reviewed: include; extracted results remain scoped

implementation.BBR_identity: Kernel/environment reported; BBRv2/v3 explicitly future work. Exact source commit not verified.

limitations: Single fixed dumbbell, deterministic traffic and loss-free links
No claim that shallow buffer improves fairness universally across versions
No BBRv3 validation; comparisons to2024ns3BBRv3study must preserve implementation difference
1Gbps host capability claim not independently profiled
Curve-level values and author repository not reproduced
High intra-group fairness can coexist with poor overall/inter-group fairness; never aggregate these metrics interchangeably
Shallow buffers may improve reported fairness but incur higher retransmission overhead
Paper has ambiguous/mistyped percentage units in Figure12 caption; do not cite caption Mbps as retransmission-ratio unit
2024 ns3 BBRv3 report and2025native-kernel report have different implementations and datasets; shared author does not prove duplicate study
review_scope: Read study motivation, methods, result sections and conclusions; Table2 visually checked. No author-code rerun or complete curve digitization.
eligibility_reason: Direct primary TCP BBR/Cubic buffer and RTT fairness study under frozen M02 criteria

table2_visual_check.scope: Ten-flow matrix aggregated by buffer categories, not individual-case BBRv3 results
